lessons.title: Talking to AI & Being Kind Online
What is AI?
lessons.content:
🤖 Imagine AI as a friendly helper robot inside your phone!
It watches what you like (videos, music, routes) and says:“Hey! I think you might like this too!”
AI can:🧭 Help you find places📸 Make your photos look better🎵 Suggest songs🗣 Turn speech into text
AI cannot:💔 Have feelings😡 Get angry🧠 Think like a human
⭐ Mini-Activity: “Robot or Human?”
Say these out loud and let participants guess!
“I love pizza!” → Human
“Calculating best route…” → Robot
“Let’s go to the beach!” → Human
“Opening Google Maps…” → Robot
💬 Fun Reminder
AI is your helper — not your boss and not your parent.You’re in charge!

quizzes.question: AI is like:🤔 A person with feelings🤖 A helpful robot in your device ✔🎈 A balloon
Can AI get sad or angry?😭 Yes😎 No ✔
Which one uses AI?📱 Google Maps ✔🍔 A cheeseburger🧹 A broom

lessons.title: Using Computers & Phones Safely
lessons.content:
😎 Be a Tech Superhero!
Your mission: Keep your device safe from bad guys online.
🛡️ Strong Password Power
A strong password is like a superhero shield:
Mix letters + numbers + symbols
Not your name or birthday
Keep it SECRET
Example: RedLion#34
🕵️‍♂️ Spy Mode: Spot the Fake Link
Fake messages say things like:
“CLICK NOW!”
“You won $1,000!”
“Urgent!!!”
Spelling mistakes everywhere
👋 If unsure, DON’T click
Ask a trusted person:Support worker, teacher, family, coordinator.
⭐ Mini-Activity: “Safe or Not Safe?”
Say “SAFE” 👍 or “NOPE!” 🚫
“Your package is ready, click here NOW!” → 🚫
“Hi, here are your photos from yesterday.” → 👍
“You won a free holiday!” → 🚫
😊 Fun Reminder
If it feels weird…STOP, don’t click, ask someone!

quizzes.question: Which one is a strong password?🐶 Dog123🦁 RedLion#34 ✔🎂 1998
Someone sends you a weird link. What do you do?👉 Click it fast👉 Send it to everyone👉❌ Ask for help or delete ✔
“You won a prize! Click!” is usually:🎉 Real🔥 Fake ✔⛄ A snowman

lessons.title: AI in Everyday Life
lessons.content:
🤯 Guess what? You use AI every day without knowing!
AI helps with:📍 Finding places on maps🎧 Recommending songs you enjoy📺 Picking shows you might like📸 Cleaning up blurry photos💬 Turning speech → text
AI is like a tiny wizard inside your apps.🧙‍♂️✨ “Here’s the best route for you!”
⭐ Mini-Activity: “Where’s the AI?”
Show participants objects or pictures and ask:Does this use AI? Yes or No?
Examples:
Google Maps → YES
Microwave → NO
Netflix → YES
Toothbrush → NO
Smartphone camera → YES
Participants can raise hands, use cards, or say “Yes/No.”
😊 Fun Reminder
AI is everywhere — it just stays quiet and helpful!

quizzes.question: Which one uses AI?🧭 Google Maps ✔🍇 Grapes🧢 A hat
AI helps with:🎧 Recommending music ✔🌲 Growing trees💰 Finding treasure
Is your camera’s auto-brighten AI?✔ Yes○ No

lessons.title: Talking to AI & Being Kind Online
lessons.content:
🗣️ Talking to AI is like talking to a friendly robot
AI chat tools can help you:
Find answers
Write messages
Make to-do lists
Explain things simply
💡 How to ask good questions
Try these:“Explain it in easy words.”“Give me three ideas.”“What does this mean?”
😇 Be kind — even online
Being polite online helps everyone feel safe.
Use:😊 “Please help me with this.”🙏 “Thank you!”👍 “Great job!”
⭐ Mini-Activity: “Ask the Robot!”
Each participant asks an AI tool a simple question like:
“What’s a fun fact?”
“What’s the weather?”
“Tell me a joke.”Everyone shares their favourite answer.
😊 Fun Reminder
AI is helpful — but double-check important things with a real person.

quizzes.question: How should you talk to AI?😡 Angry😐 Confused😊 Kindly ✔
Which question is clear?“What is stuff?”“Explain this in easy words.” ✔“???”
Should you check important info with a real person?✔ Yes○ No

lessons.title: Making a Strong Password
lessons.content:
🔐 Your password = your secret superhero identity
A strong password protects your accounts from sneaky internet villains.
What makes a strong password?
✔ At least 8 characters✔ Mix of letters (A-Z), numbers (0-9), symbols (!#$%)✔ NOT your name or birthday✔ DO NOT share with anyone except a trusted support person
Examples:
❌ Weak: 123456❌ Weak: Hasan2000✨ Strong: RedFox!82✨ Strong: MoonLight#55
⭐ Mini-Activity: “Strong or Weak?”
Say each out loud — participants call out STRONG 💪 or WEAK 🪁
Banana123
SkyBlue!44
000000
Dog#99
😊 Fun Reminder
Your password should be a secret power, not a public sign.

quizzes.question: Which is a strong password?🍕 Pizza123💪 StarLion#21 ✔🎂 2001
Should you share your password?○ Yes✔ No
Why mix letters, numbers & symbols?✔ Makes it harder to guess○ Makes it look pretty○ Makes your phone faster
options: 🧭 Be an Internet Explorer — but stay safe!
The internet = a giant world.Some places are helpful and safe…Some are confusing or dangerous.
Easy to read From trusted companies “.gov” , “.edu”, “.org” or official brands
🚫 Have LOTS of pop-up ads🚫 Flash “YOU WON A PRIZE!!!”🚫 Have spelling mistakes🚫 Ask for your details quickly
If a site feels weird…Close the tab → Ask for help.

lessons.title: Safe Searching on the Internet
lessons.content:
🌐 What is “searching online”?
Searching online means typing words into Google, YouTube, or Safari to find information, videos, maps, or answers.
Examples of safe searches:
“Weather today in Sydney”
“Easy chicken recipes”
“How to get to Kmart”
“Cute dog videos”
🔍 What makes a website SAFE?
Safe websites usually:✔ Look clean and easy to read✔ Have correct spelling✔ Don’t have too many pop-ups✔ Belong to real companies, schools, or government✔ Do NOT ask you for private information
Examples of safe endings:
.gov (government)
.edu (education)
.org (organisations)
.com.au (Australia websites)
⚠️ What makes a website UNSAFE?
Unsafe websites often:🚫 Have lots of flashing pop-ups🚫 Say “Click now!” or “You won a prize!!”🚫 Have strange spelling or weird pictures🚫 Ask for your address, bank details, or passwords🚫 Feel confusing or uncomfortable
If something feels “off”…
👉 Close the tab immediately👉 Tell a trusted person
You don’t need to explain — just say:“This website looks weird.”
⭐ Mini Activity — “Safe or Suspicious?”
Say SAFE or SUS (suspicious) for each example:
1️⃣ “education.gov.au” → SAFE2️⃣ “CLAIM YOUR FREE IPHONE!!! CLICK!!!” → SUS3️⃣ “kmart.com.au” → SAFE4️⃣ “YOU HAVE 10 SECONDS TO WIN $1,000!” → SUS
Make it fun by having participants use thumbs up (👍) or thumbs down (👎).
💬 Helpful reminder
You’re not supposed to know what every website is.If you’re unsure… STOP → CLOSE → ASK.That’s smart and safe.

quizzes.question: A safe website usually has:A. Lots of flashing pop-upsB. Correct spelling and clear layout ✔C. A big “CLICK FAST!” message
Which website ending is safe?A. .gov ✔B. .susC. .winfree
If a website feels strange, you should:A. Keep clickingB. Close it and ask for help ✔C. Type your details in

lessons.title: Using Email Safely
lessons.content:
📧 Emails are helpful — but some are TRICKS!
Fake emails try to get your info.
Safe emails are from:
✔ People you know✔ Companies you trust✔ Messages you expect to receive
Warning signs of fake emails:
🚫 Bad spelling🚫 “URGENT!” or “ACT NOW!”🚫 Asking for bank info🚫 Strange sender name
⭐ Mini-Activity: “Spot the Scam”
Read these aloud.Participants say REAL 👍 or SCAM 🚫
“Your bill is ready from your phone company.”
“CLICK FAST! Claim your free holiday!”
“Hi, here is the photo you asked for.”
😊 Fun Reminder
Real companies never ask for your password in an email.

quizzes.question: What is a sign of a fake email?✔ Spelling mistakes○ Cute emojis○ Your favourite colour
Should you give your bank info by email?○ Yes✔ No
Who should you open emails from?✔ People you know○ Random strangers○ Robots

lessons.title: Social Media Safety
lessons.content:
📱 Social media is fun — but think before you post!
Stay safe by:
✔ Keeping your account private✔ Only adding people you know✔ Using kind words✔ Posting photos that don’t show private details
Do NOT share:
🚫 Home address🚫 School/work details🚫 Bank info🚫 Personal routines
⭐ Mini-Activity: “Would You Post This?”
Participants say POST 👍 or NOPE 🚫
A selfie with your address behind you
A photo of your lunch
Your bank card
A funny picture of your pet
😊 Fun Reminder
Think: Would I show this to a stranger?If no → Don’t post it.

quizzes.question: Should you add strangers online?○ Yes✔ No
Which is safe to post?✔ A photo of your lunch○ Your bank card○ Your house address
What type of account is safest?✔ Private○ Public

lessons.title: Using AI to Help Your Everyday Life
lessons.content:
🤖 AI can make life easier — like a friendly assistant!
AI can help you:✔ Plan your day✔ Make shopping lists✔ Explain things simply✔ Write polite messages✔ Find new ideas
⭐ Try This!
Ask AI:“Give me 3 easy dinner ideas.”“Explain this in simple words.”“Make me a 3-step morning routine.”
⭐ Mini-Activity: “AI Challenge!”
Participants ask AI a question.Everyone votes on the best answer using:🏆 Useful😂 Funny🤔 Interesting
😊 Fun Reminder
AI can help — but YOU choose what to follow.

quizzes.question: AI can help you:✔ Make a list○ Brush your teeth○ Walk your dog
Which question is good to ask AI?✔ “Explain this simply.”○ “Tell me my bank password.”○ “What’s 1000 pizzas?”
Should you double-check important info?✔ Yes○ No

lessons.title: Counting Money (Notes & Coins)Lesson 2 Comparing PricesLesson 3 Adding in Real-Life SituationsLesson 4 Subtracting in Real-Life SituationsLesson 5 Understanding Time (AM & PM)Lesson 6 Reading Bus & Train TimetablesLesson 7 Measurements in Daily LifeLesson 8 Using a Calculator (Level 2)Lesson 9 Making a Small BudgetLesson 10 Daily Maths for Independence
Counting Money (Notes & Coins)
lessons.content:
Money helps you buy things, save for goals, and make smart choices.
🪙 Coins
5c, 10c, 20c, 50c, $1, $2They feel small, round, and metallic.
💵 Notes
$5, $10, $20, $50, $100They are colourful and lightweight.
Why this is important:
✔ Helps with shopping✔ Helps you count change✔ Builds independence
⭐ Interactive Activity
“Make the Amount”Ask participants to build amounts using pretend coins:
Show me $4 → $2 + $2
Show me $7 → $5 + $2
They can pick from a table or touch cards on the app.
Which is a coin?A. $20 noteB. $2 ✔C. $100 note
$5 + $5 =A. $10 ✔B. $2C. $12
Which is the smallest coin?A. $1B. 5c ✔C. 20c

lessons.title: Comparing Prices
lessons.content:
When shopping, choosing the cheaper price helps save money.
💸 Cheaper = lower number
$3 is cheaper than $6$12 is more than $7
Why this matters:
✔ Helps you stay within your budget✔ Helps you choose the best deal✔ Useful in supermarkets, online shopping, and cafes
⭐ Interactive Activity
Show two items:🍎 Apples: $4🍌 Bananas: $2Ask: “Which should we pick if we want to save money?”
Which is cheaper?A. $9B. $3 ✔C. $14
$6 is ______ than $9A. MoreB. Less ✔C. The same
If two things cost the same, they are:A. Equal ✔B. MoreC. Cheaper

lessons.title: Adding in Real-Life Situations
lessons.content:
Adding helps you see how much everything costs together.
Examples you see daily:
🍿 Snack $3 + Drink $2 = $5🚌 Bus $4 + Lunch $6 = $10🏪 Bread $2 + Eggs $4 = $6
⭐ Interactive Activity
Mini Shop Game:Participants “buy” two items and add the prices.
$2 + $3 =A. $5 ✔B. $8C. $4
$5 + $5 =A. $10 ✔B. $6C. $15
Adding helps you find:A. Total cost ✔B. ChangeC. Time

lessons.title: Subtracting in Real-Life Situations
lessons.content:
Subtracting helps you understand how much money you have left.
Real-life examples:
You have $10.You spend $4.Left: $6
If you have $20 and spend $7, you have $13 left.
⭐ Interactive Activity
Give participants $10 pretend money.Ask: “If we buy chips for $3, how much do we have left?”
$10 – $2 =A. $8 ✔B. $12C. $6
$7 – $7 =A. $0 ✔B. $3C. $14
Subtraction tells you:A. TotalB. How much is left ✔C. How much someone owes

lessons.title: Understanding Time (AM & PM)
lessons.content:
Time helps you plan your day and stay on schedule.
🕗 AM = Morning
Wake up, breakfast, school/work
🌇 PM = Afternoon/Evening
Lunch, dinner, relaxing, bedtime
⭐ Interactive Activity
Sort cards:🛏 7:00 AM → AM🍽 6:00 PM → PM
9:00 AM is:A. Morning ✔B. NightC. Midnight
7:30 PM is:A. Evening ✔B. MorningC. Afternoon
Time helps you:A. Plan your day ✔B. TeleportC. Sleep more

lessons.title: Reading Bus & Train Timetables
lessons.content:
Timetables show you when transport comes and goes.
What a timetable includes:
✔ Arrival time✔ Departure time✔ Day of week✔ Platform number
⭐ Interactive Activity
Bus arrives at 4:15 PM.Ask: “When should we be ready?”→ 4:10 PM
Timetables show:A. FoodB. Times ✔C. Movie ratings
If the bus leaves at 4:00, arrive at:A. 3:55 ✔B. 4:30C. 5:00
Timetables help you:A. Catch transport ✔B. Cook foodC. Swim

lessons.title: Measurements in Daily Life
lessons.content:
Measurement helps you cook, clean, shop, and plan.
📏 Length
cm, mExample: Your table might be 120cm.
⚖ Weight
kgExample: A bag of rice might be 2kg.
🥤 Liquids
mL, LExample: A bottle might be 600mL.
⭐ Interactive Activity
Ask: “Is a TV 50cm or 5m?”Ask: “Is a water bottle 500mL or 50L?”
kg measures:A. Weight ✔B. TimeC. Speed
1L is bigger than:A. 1000LB. 500mL ✔C. 1km
mL measures:A. Water ✔B. DistanceC. Light

lessons.title: Using a Calculator (Level 2)
lessons.content:
Calculators help when numbers feel tricky.
Buttons you will use:
add– subtract× multiply÷ divide= equals
⭐ Interactive Activity
Solve using calculator:12 – 4 =6 + 9 =20 ÷ 2 =
Participants press the buttons physically or on-screen.
“+” means:A. MultiplyB. Add ✔C. Cook
20 ÷ 2 =A. 10 ✔B. 8C. 30
Calculators help you:A. Solve maths ✔B. SleepC. Run

lessons.title: Making a Small Budget
lessons.content:
A budget is a plan for your money.
Example
You have $20.Snacks $5Drink $3Total: $8Left: $12
⭐ Interactive Activity
Give each participant pretend money ($15).Let them “buy” 2 items from a mini list.
They calculate:✔ Total✔ How much is left
A budget is a:A. Money plan ✔B. GameC. Joke
If you have $10 and spend $6, left is:A. $4 ✔B. $9C. $1
Budgeting helps you:A. Save money ✔B. Lose moneyC. Yell

lessons.title: Building a Strong Daily Routine
lessons.content:
Why routines help you
A routine makes your day easier by helping you:✔ Know what to do next✔ Feel calm and organised✔ Build independence✔ Reduce stress
Example routines
Morning:
Wake up
Brush teeth
Shower
Breakfast
Check your plan for the day
Evening:
Dinner
Shower
Pack bag
Relax
Sleep
⭐ Interactive Activity
Participants drag items to create their own morning or night routine.

lessons.title: Safe Food Handling & Simple Meal Prep
lessons.content:
Safe food habits
✔ Wash hands before touching food✔ Use clean plates and tools✔ Keep raw and cooked foods separate✔ Put food in the fridge after eating
Simple food prep examples
🥣 Making cereal🥪 Making a sandwich🍎 Washing fruit🥤 Pouring drinks
⭐ Interactive Activity
Show pictures → participants choose “SAFE” or “NOT SAFE”.

lessons.title: Cooking Easy Meals with Support
lessons.content:
Easy meals to start with
✔ Toast✔ Scrambled eggs✔ Instant noodles✔ Microwaving leftovers✔ Simple salads
Safety tips
✔ Use oven mitts✔ Keep handles turned inward✔ Ask for support for knives or hot pans
⭐ Interactive Activity
Participants choose the safest option in a cooking scenario.

lessons.title: Keeping Your Home Clean & Organised
lessons.content:
Why cleaning helps
✔ Keeps you healthy✔ Reduces stress✔ Stops bugs✔ Makes it easier to find things
Simple cleaning tasks
🛏 Make your bed🧹 Sweep or vacuum🧽 Wipe surfaces🧺 Do laundry🗑 Empty bins
⭐ Interactive Activity
Participants match tasks to the room they belong in.

lessons.title: Safe Shopping & Reading Labels
lessons.content:
Safe shopping skills
✔ Make a list✔ Check prices✔ Watch for cars✔ Stay with your support✔ Ask staff if unsure
Reading labels
Look for:✔ Price✔ Ingredients✔ Expiry date✔ Allergens (nuts, dairy, gluten)
⭐ Interactive Activity
Participants choose which label item they should check first.

lessons.title: Moving Around the Community Safely
lessons.content:
Community safety rules
✔ Look both ways✔ Don’t walk alone at night✔ Stay aware of your surroundings✔ Follow your support plan✔ Keep valuables safe
⭐ Interactive Activity
Participants choose SAFE or UNSAFE for scenarios.

lessons.title: Paying Bills & Basic Money Management
lessons.content:
Bills you may need to pay
✔ Phone✔ Internet✔ Rent✔ Electricity✔ Subscriptions
What bills include
✔ Amount✔ Due date✔ Service type
⭐ Interactive Activity
Participants find the amount and due date on a sample bill.

lessons.title: Staying Safe in Emergencies
lessons.content:
Emergencies include:
🔥 Fire🚑 Injury🚨 Feeling unsafe⚠ Flood or danger
Steps to stay safe
Stay calm
Call 000
Say your name
Say what happened
Give your location
⭐ Interactive Activity
Role-play: “Call 000 for a fire.”

lessons.title: Managing Appointments & Responsibilities
lessons.content:
Appointments include:
✔ Doctor✔ NDIS meetings✔ Support sessions✔ Centrelink✔ Therapy
Skills needed
✔ Write the date✔ Set reminders✔ Arrive on time✔ Bring documents
⭐ Interactive Activity
Participants drag appointments onto a weekly schedule.

Understanding Different Emotions
lessons.content:
What are emotions?
Emotions are signals from your body that tell you how you feel.
Common emotions
😊 Happy😢 Sad😡 Angry😰 Worried😴 Tired😃 Excited😤 Frustrated🙃 Confused
Why emotions matter
✔ Help you understand your needs✔ Help you communicate✔ Help you stay safe
⭐ Interactive Activity:
Show emotion faces → participants choose the matching word.

lessons.title: Calming My Body in Stressful Moments
lessons.content:
When your body feels upset, stressed, or overwhelmed, you can calm it down.
Calming tools
🫁 Deep breathing🧘 Stretching🧩 Fidget toys🕯 Quiet space🎧 Calm music☕ Warm drink🚶 Light walk
Why calming helps
✔ Makes your brain think clearer✔ Helps avoid meltdowns✔ Helps you make safer choices
⭐ Interactive Activity:
Participants choose their “Top 3 calming tools.”

lessons.title: Identifying Triggers & Warning Signs
lessons.content:
What is a trigger?
Something that makes your feelings get bigger or stronger.
Common triggers
🔊 Loud noise👥 Crowds🎭 Big changes⏳ Waiting too long😡 Being yelled at😕 Confusing instructions
Warning signs your body gives
🔥 Fast heartbeat🌡 Tight chest🥵 Hot face🌀 Wanting to run😤 Getting angry fast
⭐ Interactive Activity:
Participants label their own “warning signs.”

lessons.title: Healthy Ways to Cope With Stress
lessons.content:
Healthy coping skills
✔ Talking to someone✔ Drinking water✔ Deep breathing✔ Taking a break✔ Using fidgets✔ Listening to music
What are unhealthy coping skills?
❌ Yelling❌ Breaking things❌ Hurting yourself❌ Ignoring problems
⭐ Interactive Activity:
Participants sort coping tools → HEALTHY or UNHEALTHY.

lessons.title: Understanding Other People’s Feelings
lessons.content:
How people show feelings
✔ Face expressions✔ Tone of voice✔ Body posture✔ Words
Why it’s important
✔ Helps communication✔ Avoids misunderstandings✔ Helps build friendships
⭐ Interactive Activity:
Guess the emotion from voice & face examples.

lessons.title: Communicating Clearly & Kindly
lessons.content:
How to communicate kindly
✔ Use calm voice✔ Listen✔ Take turns✔ Use simple words✔ Say how you feel
Helpful phrases
“I feel upset when…”“I need some space.”“Can you help me understand this?”
⭐ Interactive Activity:
Participants change rude phrases into kind ones.

lessons.title: Managing Big Feelings Safely
lessons.content:
Big feelings include
😡 Anger😰 Anxiety😭 Sadness😤 Frustration😵 Overwhelm
Safe ways to handle big feelings
✔ Step away✔ Deep breaths✔ Ask for help✔ Go to a quiet space✔ Use calming tools
⭐ Interactive Activity:
Participants choose which tool they’d use for big feelings.

lessons.title: Solving Conflicts With Calm Choices
lessons.content:
Conflict = disagreement
Everyone has conflicts sometimes.
Calm ways to solve conflicts
✔ Listen✔ Talk clearly✔ Take turns✔ Step away if needed✔ Ask for help
⭐ Interactive Activity:
“Which is the calm solution?” game.

lessons.title: Building Confidence & Positive Self-Talk
lessons.content:
Confidence means
✔ Trusting yourself✔ Believing you can do things✔ Trying again even if mistakes happen
Positive self-talk
“I can do this.”“I’m trying my best.”“I’m learning.”
⭐ Interactive Activity:
Participants create their own positive self-talk sentence.

lessons.title: Creating Healthy Boundaries & Safe Relationships
lessons.content:
Healthy relationships include:
✔ Respect✔ Kindness✔ Personal space✔ Listening✔ Safety
Boundaries you can set
✔ “Don’t touch me.”✔ “I need space.”✔ “Please speak softly.”✔ “I don’t like that.”
⭐ Interactive Activity:
Participants choose which behaviours are healthy vs unhealthy.

lessons.title: Keeping Your Information Safe Online
lessons.content:
What is personal information?
Personal info = private details about you:
Your full name
Your address
Your phone number
Your passwords
Your bank details
Never share these online
✔ Not with strangers✔ Not with random websites✔ Not on social media✔ Not in comments or messages
Keep accounts safe by:
Using strong passwords
Keeping your account private
Logging out on shared devices
⭐ Mini Activity: “Safe or Not Safe?”
Say SAFE or NOT SAFE:
Posting your birthday 🎂
Posting your lunch 🍔
Posting your address 📍

lessons.title: Spotting Fake Messages & Scams
lessons.content:
Scams try to trick you.
Scam messages often:🚫 Say “CLICK NOW!”🚫 Offer free prizes🚫 Ask for money🚫 Pretend to be a company🚫 Have spelling mistakes
Safe messages come from:
✔ People you know✔ Real companies✔ Messages you expected
⭐ Mini Activity: “Real or Fake?”
Show examples like:
“You won a free phone!”
“Your bill is ready from Optus.”Participants choose REAL or FAKE.

lessons.title: Safe Online Shopping
lessons.content:
Online shopping is safe when:
✔ Website is real (Kmart, Target, Amazon)✔ Website ends in .com.au✔ Payment page has a lock symbol 🔒✔ You check the total cost first
Never shop on:
🚫 Random pop-up websites🚫 Social media ads that look suspicious🚫 Pages with spelling mistakes
⭐ Mini Activity: “Safe or Unsafe Shop?”
Participants vote SAFE or UNSAFE for websites you show.

lessons.title: Using Maps & GPS
lessons.content:
Maps help you:
Find places
Get directions
See travel time
Choose walking or bus routes
GPS can tell you:
✔ “Turn left”✔ “Go straight”✔ “Arrive at your destination”
⭐ Mini Activity: “Find the Place!”
Participants search for:
Nearest supermarket
Nearest hospital
Nearest train station

lessons.title: Using Voice Assistants (Siri & Google)
lessons.content:
Voice assistants help with:
✔ Alarms✔ Timers✔ Weather✔ Calling people✔ Finding information
Good questions to ask:
“What’s the weather today?”
“Set a 10-minute timer.”
“Call Mum.”
⭐ Mini Activity: “Ask the Bot!”
Participants ask the assistant 2 simple questions.

lessons.title: Emailing With Attachments
lessons.content:
Attaching files means adding:
📎 Photos📎 Documents📎 Screenshots
Before sending an attachment:
✔ Check it’s the right file✔ Check you’re sending it to the right person✔ Add a short message
⭐ Mini Activity: “Find the Attachment Icon”
Participants locate the 📎 (paperclip icon) in email apps.

lessons.title: Using Your Camera & Photos Safely
lessons.content:
Safe photo rules:
✔ No home address✔ No private info✔ No bank cards✔ No strangers’ faces
Good photo uses:
📸 Taking pictures of pets📸 Taking pictures of nature📸 Saving memories📸 Scanning documents
⭐ Mini Activity: “Safe or Not?”
Participants decide if each example photo is safe.

lessons.title: Understanding App Permissions
lessons.content:
Apps sometimes ask to:
Use your camera
Use your microphone
Access your location
Send notifications
Only allow permissions you trust.
⭐ Mini Activity: “Allow or Don’t Allow?”
Show examples like:📍 “Allow location?”🎤 “Allow microphone?”Participants choose YES or NO.

lessons.title: Fixing Simple Tech Problems
lessons.content:
Common problems:
❌ Screen frozen❌ No sound❌ Wi-Fi not working❌ App won’t open
Simple fixes:
✔ Restart device✔ Check volume✔ Check Wi-Fi✔ Close the app
⭐ Mini Activity: “What Would You Do?”
Participants match the problem to the fix.

lessons.title: Understanding My Needs & WantsLesson 2 Knowing My Rights (NDIS & Daily Life)Lesson 3 Making Safe & Smart ChoicesLesson 4 Communicating My DecisionsLesson 5 Setting Boundaries With OthersLesson 6 Asking for Help the Right WayLesson 7 Understanding Others’ FeelingsLesson 8 Solving Problems CalmlyLesson 9 Speaking Up for Myself (Self-Advocacy)Lesson 10 Being Confident in My Choices
Understanding My Needs & Wants
lessons.content:
🌟 What are “needs”?
Needs are things that help you stay healthy and safe:✔ Food✔ Water✔ Sleep✔ Medication✔ Support
🌟 What are “wants”?
Wants are things you enjoy but don’t need to survive:✔ Snacks✔ Games✔ Clothes✔ Toys✔ Eating out
Why this matters:
Understanding needs vs wants helps you:✔ Make better choices✔ Spend money wisely✔ Communicate what’s important
⭐ Interactive Activity:
Show pictures — participants sort into NEED or WANT:🍎 Food → NEED🎮 Game → WANT🏠 Shelter → NEED🍫 Chocolate → WANT

lessons.title: Knowing My Rights (NDIS & Daily Life)
lessons.content:
You have the right to:
✔ Be safe✔ Make your own choices✔ Say “no”✔ Have support✔ Be treated with respect✔ Be listened to✔ Speak up if something feels wrong
⭐ Real-life examples:
You can say:“No, I don’t want that support worker.”“I prefer a male/female worker.”“I’m not comfortable with that.”
⭐ Interactive Activity:
Choose the correct right:A support worker tells you what to eat → You can say NO and choose.

lessons.title: Making Safe & Smart Choices
lessons.content:
Safe & smart choices mean:
✔ Thinking before acting✔ Choosing what helps you✔ Avoiding danger✔ Asking for help if unsure
Examples:
❌ Walking in the road → unsafe✔ Using crossings → safe❌ Meeting strangers alone → unsafe✔ Bringing a support worker → safe
⭐ Interactive Activity:
Say SAFE or UNSAFE to scenarios shown on screen.

lessons.title: Communicating My Decisions
lessons.content:
Ways to express your choices:
✔ Using words✔ Pointing✔ Showing pictures✔ Using apps✔ Using body language
Helpful phrases:
“I choose this.”“I don’t want that.”“This makes me feel uncomfortable.”“I prefer something else.”
⭐ Interactive Activity:
Participants practice saying:→ “I choose…”→ “I don’t want…”

lessons.title: Setting Boundaries With Others
lessons.content:
Boundaries are rules that protect your space and feelings.
You can say:
✔ “Please don’t stand too close.”✔ “I need space.”✔ “Don’t touch me.”✔ “Stop. I don’t like that.”
Healthy boundaries keep you:
✔ Safe✔ Comfortable✔ Respected
⭐ Interactive Activity:
Participants choose which phrases are boundary-setting.

lessons.title: Asking for Help the Right Way
lessons.content:
Asking for help is strong, not weak.
You can ask for help when:
✔ You’re unsure✔ Something scares you✔ A task feels too hard✔ You need support or clarity
People you can ask:
✔ Support worker✔ Family✔ Trusted friend✔ Teacher✔ Coordinator
⭐ Interactive Activity:
Participants match situations with “Who can help?”

lessons.title: Understanding Others’ Feelings
lessons.content:
People show feelings using:
😊 Faces📢 Voices🧍 Body language
Why this matters:
✔ Helps avoid conflict✔ Helps build relationships✔ Helps you understand situations
⭐ Interactive Activity:
Participants choose the emotion from faces shown.

lessons.title: Solving Problems Calmly
lessons.content:
Problem-solving steps:
Stop
Breathe
Think
Choose a safe option
Ask for help if needed
Example problems:
“Someone took my seat.”“I missed the bus.”“I can’t find my phone.”
⭐ Interactive Activity:
Pick the calm response vs angry response.

lessons.title: Speaking Up for Myself (Self-Advocacy)
lessons.content:
Self-advocacy means:
✔ Saying what you need✔ Asking questions✔ Saying “no”✔ Telling people your preferences
Helpful phrases:
“I need help understanding this.”“This doesn’t feel safe.”“I want something different.”
⭐ Interactive Activity:
Participants role-play asking for what they need.
